title: Regionally-weighted model availability heatmap and procurement oscillator playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a repeatable playbook and dashboard (heatmap + oscillator) that scores regional model availability and procurement sensitivity. The artifact will combine telemetry (latency, availability, price) with qualitative signals (vendor cadence, licensing friction, quant-compatibility) into a time-series oscillator that surfaces when to trigger procurement actions (reserve capacity, negotiate pricing, onboard a fallback model). Goal is to give Sales/Procurement/SRE a single signal for proactive sourcing and renewal negotiation guidance.
acceptance_criteria: Heatmap prototype exists covering NA/EU/APAC with normalized metrics for latency, availability, cost, and quant-compatibility
Oscillator algorithm defined, documented, and implemented in a lightweight notebook with explained weighting choices
Playbook includes three procurement-trigger thresholds (monitor, engage, commit) and recommended operational steps for each
Dashboard links to canonical artifacts (evaluation harness, synthetic workload results, vendor dossiers) and is accessible to GTM stakeholders
Pilot run with two enterprise accounts and two internal product teams completed and feedback captured
tasks: Define signal taxonomy and normalization scheme (telemetry, procurement, qualitative)
Prototype oscillator scoring function (exponential smoothing + volatility penalty)
Collect vendor-level inputs: published latency SLAs, historical availability, regional capacity signals
Instrument synthetic workload runner to collect comparable latency/cost across candidate models
Design dashboard wireframe and metrics drilldown (Console team collaboration)
Write procurement playbook with step-by-step actions for monitor/engage/commit thresholds
Coordinate pilot with two Sales reps and Procurement lead; schedule demos and feedback loop
Document limitations and recommended cadence for signal re-tuning
notes: We're intentionally weighting availability higher in regulated markets (EU finserv) and cost higher for SMB territories. Oscillator will be implemented as a decoupled service to allow backfill with live telemetry or synthetic runner outputs. Trade-offs discussed: heavier smoothing reduces false positives but delays procurement actions; chosen initial smoothing window is 14 days.
